key_insight: Apparent gains in drug-target forecasting may reflect access to future trial records rather than genuine predictive ability.
clinical_relevance: Reliable target prioritisation could inform which hypotheses enter costly clinical trials, but this study cautions against interpreting leaked outcomes as forecasting success.
method: Defined each target–disease event as the pair’s first clinical trial.
Reconstructed year-end biomedical knowledge graphs from 2020 onward.
Tested six open language models with and without graph retrieval against a trial-history baseline.
evidence_signal: Pre-decision evidence added at most small gains, while the newest graph clearly lifted five of six models above baseline but usually included the target–disease pair’s own future trial.
watch_item: Evaluations must restrict evidence to information available before the decision and assess outcomes occurring afterward to prevent temporal leakage.
paper_title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
